articles.title: Elon Musk told ex-girlfriend he needed ‘a legion of children before the civil war’
articles.summary: Ashley St Clair was speaking at the Venice film premiere of Alex Gibney’s documentary Musk, where she warned of his dangerous influence. • Musk review – epic study of the world’s richest and most banal man.
body: Elon Musk is sowing “deliberate division” via his social media platform X that will be catastrophic unless regulated, the mother of one of the 14 confirmed children fathered by the world’s richest man has warned.

In Musk, a new documentary by veteran film-maker Alex Gibney, former Maga influencer Ashley St Clair says Musk told her in a text message he wanted to have a child with her because he needed to have “a legion of children before the civil war”.

The couple had a son in 2024 but have since separated. St Clair says Musk’s team offered her a $40m lump-sum payment and a monthly stipend of $100,000 in return for her signing a non-disclosure agreement but withdrew the offer after she refused to sign it.

Asked at the documentary’s Venice film festival premiere whether her ex-partner was just scared of a civil war or actively trying to stoke one, St Clair said: “Whatever it is, what he’s doing with this platform on X cannot be ignored, because he is stoking flames that don’t exist in the real world.”
points: Ashley St Clair was speaking at the Venice film premiere of Alex Gibney’s documentary Musk, where she warned of his dangerous influence.

articles.title: State handouts, 10,000 lasers – and Trump’s election: six things we learned from the Elon Musk film
articles.summary: Alex Gibney’s marathon documentary delivers numerous eye-raising insights into the broligarch’s business deals, early idealism and apocalyptic appetite for fathering children.
body: Veteran documentarian Alex Gibney’s film about the richest broligarch on the planet has been one of the most eagerly anticipated films at the Venice film festival this year. The Oscar-winning 72-year-old, who has in previous films taken on the US military, the Catholic church, Vladimir Putin and Scientology, has been investigating the tech tycoon’s ascent and speaking to people in his orbit since late 2022, before his Maga turn and Trump 2.0.

Recently, Musk has held forth at length about his view that “suicidal empathy” – people who have more empathy for criminals than the victims of criminals, in his view – is behind the decline of western civilisation. Empathy isn’t bad, he says in the doc, it’s just that it’s become too shallow. But interviews in the film raise the question of whether Musk is capable of empathy at all. This is a man who tells his wife that “if you were my employee, I would fire you”, and urges her to tell his estranged trans-daughter Jenna that “I’ll always love her” – and then cuts off her health insurance the next day.
points: Alex Gibney’s marathon documentary delivers numerous eye-raising insights into the broligarch’s business deals, early idealism and apocalyptic appetite for fathering children.

articles.title: Musk review – epic study of the world’s richest and most banal man
articles.summary: Venice film festival: Alex Gibney interviews former colleagues, wives, the trillionaire’s father and a CG avatar in this absorbing documentary. ‘Elon is a nuke.” The speaker is Ashley St Clair, a former conservative Maga influencer and one of Elon Musk’s former girlfriends-slash-baby mommas.
body: She is a fascinating expert witness in Alex Gibney’s four-hour epic study of the world’s richest and dullest man: the overgrown brattish South-African-born trillionaire plutocrat, ersatz visionary and Trump courtier who owns Tesla cars, SpaceX rocket ships, Starlink satellites on which nation states’ military capabilities are increasingly reliant, X (formerly Twitter) which shapes the collective “incel” id of billions and GrokAI whose vast server farms daily guzzle oceans of precious water.

As head of Trump’s incompetent cost-cutting Doge (Department of Government Efficiency) unit, Musk actually increased the US deficit by sacking thousands of revenue officers whose job was to rake in tax – while reportedly accessing and improperly sharing Americans’ sensitive social security data.
He does indeed look like a nuke, efficiently designed, destructive, seemingly unguided and uncontrolled.

Gibney’s excellent film covers a lot of ground in its extraordinary story, although we don’t get to hear about the mysterious process that changed a balding youngster into a follicularly unchallenged mature man.

articles.title: Just an Illusion review – Louis Garrel and Camille Cottin sizzle as an 80s couple in crisis
articles.summary: The directing duo behind uplifting mega-hit Intouchables return for this heartwarming coming-of-age drama, but it is the parents in the story who pull focus. Olivier Nakache and Éric Toledano are the French directors who created the uplifting mega-hit Intouchables, about a wealthy quadriplegic and…
body: The film opens with Vincent (Simon Boublil) preparing for his barmitzvah against a fractious atmosphere at home. The country is gripped by recession and money is tight. His dad, Yves (Garrel) was laid off months ago, but every morning puts on a suit and pretends to go out to work; Garrel is terrific, likable but fundamentally unreliable. Vincent’s mum is a go-getting secretary, who can see that the future is technology and signs up for an IT course. At school, Vincent has a massive crush on a girl who cannot remember his name, or chooses not to – she calls him “Thingummy”.

articles.title: ‘Littermates’ Sets Theatrical Release Via Alamo Exclusives; Comic Dystopian Film Also Sets Fantastic Fest Screening (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Scott Tinkham and Michael Woloson’s indie feature “Littermates” is headed to the big screen. The comic dystopian feature is set to open at over 30 Alamo Drafthouse locations on Nov. 6 via Alamo Exclusives. The film will also have a special presentation screening at Fantastic Fest on Sept.
body: “We made ‘Littermates’ to explore the strange, primal and often trivial relationship between siblings. At its heart, the film is an unconventional coming-of-age story set against a dystopian backdrop,” directors Scott Tinkham and Michael Woloson said in a statement. “We always imagined the film as something to experience with a crowd, so introducing it at Fantastic Fest and then bringing it to audiences around the country through Alamo Exclusives feels like the perfect way to start this next chapter.”
“Littermates” is the second film from Alamo Exclusives, following the documentary “Butthole Surfers: The Hole Truth and Nothing Butt.”

“’Littermates’ is exactly the kind of discovery Alamo Exclusives exists to champion. It’s funny, audacious, visually confident and nearly impossible to fit inside a conventional box,” Michael Kustermann, CEO of Alamo Drafthouse Cinema, said in a statement. “Through deadpan social absurdity and unnerving family dynamics, Scott and Michael have created a strange little world that is entirely their own. I can’t wait to introduce it to the Fantastic Fest fiends before bringing it to Alamo Drafthouse theaters nationwide.”

articles.title: The New Chris Rock: The Comedy Icon on Directing ‘Misty Green’ and Not Returning to the Oscars Unless He’s Nominated
articles.summary: Chris Rock isn’t exactly who you remember him to be. He likes to take his time. “What am I trying to say?” he asks himself repeatedly in conversation, pausing to truly consider that question before continuing to speak. And he doesn’t speak at all on an empty stomach.
body: That isn’t to say he’s shed the opinionated, incendiary persona that caught Eddie Murphy’s eye at a New York comedy club one night when Rock was just 19, leading to his being cast in Murphy’s “Beverly Hills Cop II” (1987) and later “Saturday Night Live” (1990-93). Rock was one of the few celebrities to publicly predict Donald Trump would win the 2016 election, and speaking about the president today, Rock says, “I’m not a fan. But it’s weird when somebody gets one thing right, and the one thing almost clears them of all their other sins. The news is fake. He got that right.”

Still, Rock has formed a habit of making concessions to his least generous interpreters before anyone has even criticized him. “People have their reasons, and nobody’s wrong,” he says after remarking that it’s difficult to find actresses interested in roles that involve nudity. Referencing some Black actors’ grievances about the prevalence of Brits and nepo babies in Hollywood — a position he disagrees with and satirizes in his upcoming film “ Misty Green ” — he says, “They’re valid. I’m not going to dismiss anyone.”

articles.title: FKA Twigs Begins Shoot as Josephine Baker in Studiocanal Biopic (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Grammy-winning artist FKA Twigs has begun principal photography as the legendary entertainer and activist Josephine Baker. Production on “Josephine Baker” has kicked off in France and will run through Nov. 13, with additional shooting in Sofia, Bulgaria.
body: The film traces Baker’s arc from a childhood marked by racial segregation in the United States to her breakthrough as one of the most celebrated stage and screen performers of 1920s Paris, through her service with the French Resistance during the Second World War, and into her 1951 return to America – where she confronted a country still shaped by the injustices she had fled decades earlier.

FKA Twigs brings a cross-disciplinary background to the role. A singer-songwriter, dancer-choreographer and visual artist, she broke into film with Alma Har’el’s “Honey Boy” and has since appeared in Rupert Sanders’ “The Crow” and David Lowery’s A24 feature “Mother Mary,” opposite Anne Hathaway and Michaela Coel.

articles.title: 'I didn't want to leave The Voice', says Sir Tom Jones
articles.summary: The Welsh singer has appeared as an on-off coach on the competition since it premiered in 2012.
body: Sir Tom Jones has said ITV "fired" him as a judge on The Voice, and he did not want to leave as he "loves the show".
The 86-year-old singer from Treforest in Pontypridd, Rhondda Cynon Taf, has appeared as an on-off coach on the singing competition since it premiered in 2012.
Following rumours that he may not return to the panel for the upcoming series, Sir Tom said the broadcaster decided a while ago, but he "was told recently".
He said on social media that he had been offered a reduced role - one he was "not thrilled" about.

articles.title: Four Renoir paintings worth millions stolen in French museum heist
articles.summary: It is the latest in a string of high-profile art thefts in Europe that has again put the security of museums and galleries in the spotlight.
body: Four paintings by the impressionist artist Pierre-Auguste Renoir have been stolen from a museum in the south of France.
Two thieves broke into the Renoir Museum in Cagnes-sur-Mer on Tuesday morning but dropped two of the paintings in the institution's garden as they made their escape, local Mayor Bryan Masson said.

The paintings, each worth €9m (£7.7m; $10.4m), are the latest high-profile pieces to have been stolen in a string of recent heists in Europe which have thrust the security of art in galleries and museums into the spotlight.
One of the most high-profile was in October last year, when a brazen heist at the Louvre Museum in Paris saw France's priceless crown jewels being stolen.

articles.title: Sixth Season of “Slow Horses” Stands Out in Crowded TV Season
articles.summary: There’s no 6-episode anything on television this year that hums like the sixth season of “Slow Horses,” an outing that’s entertaining, suspenseful, and honestly moving.
body: One of Apple TV’s best shows, “Slow Horses,” bounces back after a relatively down fifth season to deliver to fans what might be its best outing to date. More than anything, this adaptation of two Mick Herron books ( Joe Country and Slough House ) counters the current epidemic of streaming television wherein so many limited series feel like they should have just been a movie. How many times lately have you seen two hours of plot in an 8-episode box? It’s driving TV critics like yours truly slowly insane.

Of course, as is often the case with a season of “Slow Horses,” much of the joy is in how the complex plotting unfolds, so this review will be vague. It’s one of those shows in which it feels like the writers are always just a step ahead of the viewer, but it makes you sit forward to catch up instead of the common reaction to streaming originals of scrolling on your phone until something happens.
